Prepares the audio for BirdNET

Source: R/birdnet.R
prepare_audio.Rd

BirdNET works with mono audio at 48 kHz. Recordings that already are so are used as they are; the others (e.g. AudioMoth at 250 kHz or stereo) are converted with ffmpeg into <output>/audio_48k/. Triggered recordings (*T.WAV) are expanded first, restoring their silences, so that the times of the detections are right. Recordings that are not valid (column problem) are left out.

Usage

prepare_audio(am)

Arguments

am

Object created with read_audiomoth().

Value

am with the column birdnet_path (audio read by BirdNET) in am$recordings.

Details

This step is optional: analyze_birdnet() converts by itself, just before analysing them, the recordings that still need it (and only those without a result yet, so the converted copies can be deleted once the analysis is finished).

Examples

card <- system.file("extdata", "example", "card", package = "AudiomothR")
am <- read_audiomoth(card, coordinates = "41.00, -3.00", output = tempfile())
#> 
#> ── AudioMoth FACADE0012345678 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> • Folder: /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/AudiomothR/extdata/example/card
#> • Site of this card: AudioMoth FACADE0012345678 (41, -3; ±698 m; source:
#> argument)
#> • Map: <https://www.openstreetmap.org/?mlat=41&mlon=-3#map=15/41/-3>
#> • Recordings: 16 in 2 days (2026-10-07 to 2026-10-15, Europe/Madrid time)
#> • Audio: 48,000 Hz, gain Medium, 0.7 min in total
#> • 10 with problems: duration < 3 s
#> • Battery: 4.9 V → 4.5 V
#> • Temperature: 11.7 to 34.4 °C
#> • Results in: /tmp/RtmpoqZwSo/file22a728868a1e
am <- prepare_audio(am)   # 48 kHz mono already: nothing to convert
#> ✔ All valid recordings are already 48 kHz mono: nothing to convert.
#> ! 10 recordings with problems are left out (see column problem).
